text:
maria: Quick dump of an experiment from this morning — running LLM-34B-v2 through AWQ, GPTQ, and native FP8 on staging with prefix cache + continuous batching. Seeing unexpected latency spikes when cache hit rate is ~55-70% and concurrency climbs > 80.
aditya: Can you paste the perf numbers? p50/p95/p99 and hit rate samples?
maria: Yep. Full run attached below (trimmed). Note the p99 jump as hit rate drops slightly due to eviction churn.
```
model      quant   cache_hit  p50_ms  p95_ms  p99_ms  notes
LLM-34B-v2 AWQ     0.68       40      120     420     spikes correlate w/ cache refills
LLM-34B-v2 GPTQ    0.71       36      110     190     more stable tail
LLM-34B-v2 FP8     0.80       34       95     160     best latency but higher mem

batching: continuous batching ON, batch_timeout=8ms, max_batch_tokens=4096, concurrency ~ 85
```

devon: Two quick thoughts — 1) AWQ may have slightly different KV cache behavior post-quant; cached key mismatch/serialization rounding can increase cache churn. 2) Continuous batching with low timeout means we sometimes combine requests with stale prefixes causing suboptimal kernel paths.
sarah: Noted. Did you repro with prefetch disabled? And what's the prefix cache TTL / LRU window?
maria: Prefetch was enabled (default) for these runs. TTL effectively ~ 20s given our traffic and 12GB prefix cache size; eviction rate ~ 0.9%/min. When eviction spikes (small burst) hit rate drops 10-15% and p99 climbs 2-3x for AWQ.
aditya: Could be quant-specific decoding path that forces fallback kernels when batch contains mixed cached vs non-cached sequences. We should try two controlled runs: (A) AWQ + cache disabled; (B) AWQ + cache enabled but batching forced to micro-batches (timeout=0, cap=1) to remove kernel mixing.
maria: I ran (A) and (B) earlier:
```
A) AWQ + cache disabled => p50 38ms, p95 130ms, p99 180ms (much more stable than with cache)
B) AWQ + micro-batch => p50 42ms, p95 125ms, p99 200ms (stable, lower spikes)
```
eval-bot: Alert: quality regression detected on eval-suite-v3 for AWQ cached runs — ~1.8% delta on long-context summarization (ROUGE-L).
sarah: Important. Is the quality delta only when cache hits happen or across the board?
maria: Preliminary signal shows the regression manifests primarily on cache-hit requests that were later evicted and re-prefetched — i.e., the same prompt served from a different kernel/quant state. Suspect non-determinism in AWQ's dequant/rounding + cache serialization.
aditya: Then two separate axes: latency instability (cache+batching interplay) and accuracy drift (cache persistence + quant rounding). Both need targeted fixes. Short-term: disable prefix cache for AWQ models in production or bump cache TTL to reduce churn. Medium-term: ensure cache keys include quantization fingerprint and unify serialization.
devon: Agree. Also consider adding a small batching guard: if cache_hit_ratio between 50-80% and concurrency > 60, force conservative batching (increase timeout or cap batch size) to avoid mixing kernel types.
maria: Proposed config to test (canary on staging 10% traffic):
```yaml
model_profile:
  name: LLM-34B-v2-AWQ-canary
  quant: AWQ
  prefix_cache:
    enabled: true
    ttl_s: 120   # increase from 20s
    include_quant_fingerprint: false  # TODO: flip true after serialization fix
  batching:
    mode: adaptive
    batch_timeout_ms: 20
    max_batch_tokens: 2048
    guard_rules:
      - when: cache_hit_ratio in [0.5,0.8] and concurrency > 60
        action: set batch_timeout_ms: 40
```
sarah: LGTM. Can you add the quant fingerprint toggle to the middleware PR? That's the only reliable long-term fix.
aditya: I'll pick up the serialization + fingerprint work. Plan: add sha256 of quant params to cache key, and round-trip test on staging with deterministic seeds.
maria: Action items:
- aditya: add quant fingerprint to cache key + unit tests (ETA 2d)
- devon: implement batching guard rule in runtime (ETA 3d)
- sarah: schedule canary and add eval-suite run to CI for regression checks (ETA 1d)
- maria: run extended traffic sims to validate tail and eviction patterns (ETA 2d)
sarah: Thanks. For the canary, let's limit AWQ traffic to non-sensitive customers until quality signal is green. :ok_hand:
maria: I'll post follow-up with updated numbers after the fingerprint patch lands. Thanks all! :rocket!
